title: XNOR Exclusive-NOR Gate (IC 74266)
summary: An XNOR gate (Exclusive-NOR) produces a HIGH (1) output IF AND ONLY IF the inputs are EQUAL (both 0 or both 1). It is also known as a Digital Equivalence Gate or Comparator.

images.caption: IC 74266 Quad 2-Input XNOR Gate on breadboard.

working_principle: The XNOR gate evaluates Y = (A ⊕ B)' = A·B + A'·B'. Output is 1 when A=0, B=0 OR A=1, B=1.
applications: Digital Equality Comparators (Output 1 when A equals B)
advantages: Directly tests equality between binary signals
disadvantages: IC 74266 features open-collector outputs requiring external pull-up resistors in real hardware
common_mistakes: Forgetting pull-up resistors on IC 74266 open-collector outputs in physical lab circuits.
quick_notes: Pin 14 is VCC (+5V), Pin 7 is GND.
XNOR outputs 1 when inputs are equal.

viva_questions.q: Why is an XNOR gate called a Digital Comparator?
viva_questions.a: Because its output is HIGH (1) whenever both inputs are equal in value (both 0 or both 1).

interview_questions.q: How can you construct an XNOR gate using only NOR gates?
interview_questions.a: Pass inputs A and B into a 4-NOR gate network.
